# node-type-surface fixture

A two-project workspace whose projects resolve DIFFERENT copies of `@types/node`, both real packages: the entry project (`app/`) is typed by the old-layout `@types/node` 24.13.3 vendored under `tests/fixtures/node-types/node_modules` (the harness links it in as `app/node_modules` at test time), and the reached library project (`lib/`) carries its own `node_modules/@types/node` 26.1.2 with `undici-types` 8.3.0, committed here as test data pinned like the other vendored fixtures. The old layout declares `node:events`, `child_process` and `net` one way round; the new layout (`@types/node` 25 and later) declares them the other way: `declare module "node:child_process"` is the primary module and `"child_process"` re-exports it, `ChildProcess` and `net.Server` are `class X implements EventEmitter` merged with `interface X extends InternalEventEmitter<...>`, and `node:events` owns the `export =`.

What the fixture pins (see `tests/harness/node-type-surface.test.ts`):

- One copy of each ambient Node type package per program: the newest copy any reached project resolves wins (26.1.2 here), and the other copy stands down. Loading both layouts into one checker program merges `node:events` with two `export =` assignments and `child_process`/`node:child_process` with each other's re-exports; under the forced `skipLibCheck` that collision surfaced only as user-site errors ("Property 'on' does not exist on type 'ChildProcess'", the same for `once`/`off` and for `net.Server`). With the rule, `app/main.ts` attaches `child.on`/`child.once`/`server.on`/`server.once` listeners, preflight passes, and the compiled binary matches Node on both first-class targets.
- `app/off.ts` attaches `server.off` and `child.off` listeners: preflight passes under the one copy, and the Rust lane's verdict on those members (an SC2020 refusal) is pinned.
- `app/removed.ts` calls `util.isDate`, which 24.13.3 declares and 26.1.2 dropped: a project checked against a different copy than its own tsconfig resolves gets an honest `SC0001` for the missing export, carrying a hint that names both copies. A type mismatch the Node declarations cannot explain, in the same file, carries no hint.
